//: Advisories the dependency audit is allowed to ignore, and only until the date
on each entry. Every field is required and every one is enforced by
scripts/audit-check.mjs:
id       the GHSA or CVE identifier, or the package name for an advisory
that has neither.
reason   why shipping with it is acceptable. 'not exploitable here' is not
a reason; say which code path is or is not reached.
expires  ISO date. ON AND AFTER THIS DATE THE BUILD FAILS, whether or not
the advisory is still open. An allowlist that never expires is a
permanent exception with a comment attached, which is how a known
vulnerability becomes a forgotten one. Renewing an entry is a
deliberate act with a fresh reason.
Empty as of 2026-08-02, and empty is the intended resting state.
The four entries that used to live here, one vitest and three vite, all rested
on the same sentence: the fix needs vite 7 and vitest 3, that upgrade hits a
peer conflict with @vitejs/plugin-react, and it is a migration rather than a
line in a security commit. The reachability arguments were sound and are worth
reading in the git history. The upgrade claim was not, and it was checkable on
the day it was written.
The advisories are fixed in vite 6.4.3, not vite 7. @vitejs/plugin-react 5
peers vite ^4 || ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8, so the peer conflict belonged to
plugin-react 4 and disappears one major up. vite 5.4.10 to 6.4.3, vitest 2 to
3.2.7, plugin-react 4 to 5.2.0. npm audit goes from 10 advisories, including
two critical, to zero. The console still builds and all 275 tests still pass.
Worth keeping: dev-only reachability is a good argument, and it is not a reason
to stop looking for a fix. These four sat behind an unverified sentence about a
major version for months, and nothing in this mechanism could have caught that,
because the mechanism only ever asks whether the reason is still in date, never
whether it is still true.
